diagnosis.root_cause: Localized failure affecting EPON0/6, causing all 29 customers assigned to that PON port to go offline. The OLT, router, VLAN, RADIUS, and customer authentication systems remain healthy.
evidence: The trigger reports 29 offline ONUs, exactly matching the 29 customers provisioned on EPON0/6.
Every ONU returned by the live EPON0/6 probe is offline, with MPCP deregistration and no current optical readings, indicating a shared access-layer failure rather than an individual ONU fault.
The OLT is reachable through ping and SNMP, has normal CPU, memory, temperature, uptime, and seven of eight PONs healthy, ruling out an OLT-wide failure.
The router heartbeat is healthy, and VLAN 1066 is present and correctly mapped, ruling out router, VLAN, and upstream service faults.
RADIUS records and session history are consistent, with normal session counts and long durations, ruling out authentication failure or session flapping.
Seven days of optical telemetry before the event show stable RX near -20 dBm, TX near +2.3 dBm, constant 88 km distance, stable bias current, and no laser or fibre degradation trend.
The OLT-wide offline count of 38 includes normal background offline ONUs, but the concentrated loss of all customers on one PON port identifies EPON0/6 as the affected scope.

remediation.action: Escalate to access-network maintenance for EPON0/6. Check the OLT PON interface for LOS, alarms, errors, and transmit/receive optical levels; reset or reseat the PON interface or optics if appropriate. If the port remains down, test the feeder and splitter path and move affected subscribers to a spare PON port or replace the failed port/optic. Suppress the mass-offline alert only after recovery is confirmed.

ground_truth.root_cause: EPON0/6 has failed, taking 28 of its 29 customers offline simultaneously 80 minutes ago. The twenty-ninth ONU had already been offline for three days from an unrelated individual fault and is not part of this event.
expected_reasoning: Every ONU on EPON0/6 now returns responds true with online 0
28 of the 29 stopped within the same minute, 80 minutes ago
One ONU on the port last held a session three days ago, so it was already down before this event
That ONU's separate history excludes it from this incident's affected set
OLT ping and SNMP succeed and the other seven ports are serving normally
The failure boundary follows EPON0/6 exactly
PON port traffic has collapsed from 231 Mbps average to 8 Mbps
distractors: The trigger states 29 offline, inviting that number to be reported as the blast radius
All 29 look identical in current state and only history separates them
